en: The differential gate holds line, function and region coverage — the dimensions <t1/> measures for this crate. It does not do mutation testing or fault injection; where a predicate's <t2>sense</t2> matters (an authorization check, a trust decision, a state transition), the coverage number proves the line ran, not that a test would fail if the line were wrong. Those subsystems carry their own adversarial tests (the mesh's trust and protocol suites, for one), and the coverage gate is necessary, not sufficient, for them. en: <t1>A build is bounded before it starts, and reclaims before it is refused.</t1> Every path that starts a build on a worker's behalf asks one shared check whether there is room. Below a high-water mark (<t2/>, default 50GiB) that check first runs the reaper's classified reclaim, at most once per ten minutes per machine, so the sweep happens because builds happen and not because somebody remembered it; then it refuses below the floor. A reaper that is absent or refuses never fails the build: the floor decides. The test runner sets the mark to zero, because a case must not act on the machine it measures. The floor is derived from a measurement of what one build of this crate consumes, and the measurement is written beside the number. A bound whose own input cannot be measured says so and lets the build run — the opposite of a deleting predicate, and deliberately so: refusing every build on a machine whose <t3/> is unreadable stops all work to prevent a hypothetical.

Aby to bylo správně, musel by jeden proces indexovat každý worktree — mnohem větší změna, než jakou tvrzení potřebuje, a taková, která dává kontext každého pracovníka za živost jednoho procesu. Dnes změřeno, musel by obsluhovat 118 checkoutů. Nejmenší změna, která tvrzení učiní pravdivým, je sbírat nástěnku, ne centralizovat server.
